lines:
Responsibilities: Owns the durable machine-local operational companion for an active Chat whose ChatHistoryBindingV1 selects PortableProject. Portable semantic history remains canonical only in immutable JSONL/CAS. This journal preserves the exact local binding, delivery, deduplication, process, and recovery facts required to continue the already-bound Run after a core, worker, host, or power failure without inventing a second history or replay permission.

Owned records/files: PortableRuntimeJournalEntryV1 is a schema-versioned integrity-hashed SQLite envelope. It contains a PendingPortableCommit or HeadLinked commit link, an optional content-addressed full FrozenRunSnapshotV1 reference/bytes, the local AuthorityManifestV1 and authority decisions, CredentialRef values only, pending approval records, queued-input delivery records, command and invocation deduplication records including any settled CapabilityOutcomeV1 needed for idempotent return, capability-dispatch and worker-control outboxes, WorkerCheckpointV1 bytes/reference, process and channel generations, delivery watermarks, and the recovery cursor. A commit link stores CommitId, expected and proposed portable head hashes, prepared portable object hashes/reference, request hash, PortableCheckpointRecordV1 hash/reference, and the verified PortableCommitReceiptV1. It never stores a SemanticEvent or CoreEventEnvelopeV1 stream, a LocalLedgerCheckpointV1, or canonical PortableCheckpointRecordV1 bytes.

Stable keys and fencing: The primary identity is ChatId + BranchId + CommitId + MachineInstanceId + BindingGeneration. ExpectedHeadHash, ProposedHeadHash, FrozenSnapshotHash, authority-manifest hash, WorkerCheckpointV1 hash, process generation, outbox/dedup IDs, and monotonic delivery/recovery cursors are compared as fences rather than inferred from timestamps. Reusing an ID with different content is corruption. Per-Chat and per-branch writes serialize under expected journal generation; stale worker, host, process, binding, and restore generations are rejected.

Ports and access: The sealed PortableRuntimeJournalWritePort exposes BeginPortableCommit, FinalizeHeadLinked, RecordRuntimeMutation, MarkDelivery, QuarantineBinding, and MarkTerminal solely to aworkit.trusted_core.event_committer. BeginPortableCommit accepts the prepared portable commit identity plus all same-transition operational mutations and returns only after the SQLite transaction is durable. FinalizeHeadLinked accepts only an independently verified portable receipt. The read-only PortableRuntimeRecoveryReadPort exposes LoadRuntimeState, ListPendingPortableCommits, VerifyDedupIdentity, ListPendingDelivery, and ReadRecoveryCursor solely to aworkit.trusted_core.recovery, which requests any mutation through the event committer. PortableRuntimeJournalMaintenancePort is available only to the local storage coordinator for schema, integrity, backup/restore, and retention mechanics. There is no UI, worker, capability-host, plugin, or portable-store port.

Write ordering and acknowledgement: The event committer first obtains an exact PreparedPortableCommitV1 with content hashes but no published branch-head ref. It then durably writes PendingPortableCommit and the related local snapshot, authority, deduplication, approval/input, outbox, generation, and cursor mutations in one journal transaction. Only after that receipt may it publish the prepared portable head through the Portable Commit Coordinator. It verifies CommitId, proposed head hash, parent head, branch, and PortableCheckpointRecordV1 hash from a fresh portable read, then atomically changes the matching journal entry to HeadLinked and releases delivery eligibility. CoreCommittedAckV1, committed CapabilityOutcomeV1 delivery, worker control, or capability dispatch is released only after both the portable head and HeadLinked journal transaction are durable and mutually consistent.

Crash reconciliation: A crash before the pending transaction leaves no journal claim and no acknowledgement; any unreferenced prepared portable objects remain delayed orphan candidates. A crash after PendingPortableCommit but before head publication is reconciled by exact CommitId, expected/proposed head hashes, request hash, prepared-object hashes, machine identity, and binding generation. If the expected head is unchanged, the event committer may resume only that exact prepared publication; it never regenerates semantic events or repeats a model, tool, shell, file, MCP, plugin, or external-agent effect. A crash after portable head publication but before local finalization is resolved by VerifyCommitIdentity and an idempotent FinalizeHeadLinked. A crash after HeadLinked but before delivery re-emits only the same generation-fenced outbox item at its durable cursor. Missing proof, a different head, branch ambiguity, content mismatch, or binding-generation drift quarantines the entry and blocks continuation instead of guessing, rebasing, merging, silently adapting, or replaying an effect.

Absence, invalidation, expiry, and retention: Exact reconciliation of MachineInstanceId, BindingGeneration, ChatId, BranchId, CommitId, the verified portable head, and all journal fences on the same installation is the only path that preserves and resumes the original Chat/Run identity. A portable import or checkout on another machine normally has no matching journal. Its history is inert; continuation requires explicit local rebinding, a new MachineInstanceId/BindingGeneration, a newly resolved FrozenRunSnapshotV1 and authority manifest, and fresh approvals where required. Successful rebinding creates a new child Chat/Run and portable branch linked to the verified source checkpoint; it never converts the imported runtime into the old active Run. No authority or pending approval is inherited. CredentialRef invalidation, capability/extension/workspace drift, restored-backup generation mismatch, or portable head mismatch blocks and quarantines the old binding. Only terminal or explicitly superseded records with no PendingPortableCommit, undelivered outbox, unresolved approval/input, or uncertain invocation may be compacted after a configurable safety horizon. Quarantined evidence is retained until an explicit validated disposition. Backup restore re-verifies machine identity, BindingGeneration, the current portable head, and every journal fence before any row can become active; a copied backup cannot transfer Run identity or authority.

Security and reliability: The journal is excluded from portable export and Git, protected with desktop-user filesystem permissions and SQLite integrity checks, and contains no credential values, secret lease material, hidden reasoning, unredacted protocol frames, executable plugin code, provider-native objects, or Rig-native state. Opaque CredentialRef values are never resolved here. Disk-full, corruption, unsupported schema, failed fsync, or quota exhaustion closes the portable-runtime write gate while leaving canonical portable history inspectable. Backup copies remain machine-local operational data and cannot grant authority when copied.

Performance and observability: WAL transactions, composite indexes on ChatId/BranchId/phase and outbox/dedup state, content-addressed snapshot deduplication, bounded batches and payload sizes, and per-Chat serialization keep normal writes incremental. The writer applies backpressure before the portable head can advance when the journal is unavailable. Metrics expose pending age, finalize latency, outbox depth, recovery scans, generation/head mismatches, quarantine count, fsync latency, and compaction volume without logging sensitive payloads.

Non-responsibilities: It does not select the canonical backend, own or project semantic history, write portable JSONL/CAS or Git state, decide authority or approvals, resolve credentials, execute or dispatch effects, supervise processes, schedule workflows, repair portable history, merge branches, acknowledge workers directly, or make an imported session runnable.

data.name: Portable Run Runtime Journal
data.technology: Rust SQLite repository with WAL, durable transactions, content-addressed local snapshot blobs, integrity hashes, and bounded outboxes
